body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Omniscient One.

body.text: 1. evam mayā śrutam, ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma (

children.text: ) jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham ardhatrayodaśabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ //
children.translated_text: in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> — twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.translated_text: 1. Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>) was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>,

body.text: 2. tatra khalu bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma / anityatā bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārā adhruvā anāsvāsikā vipariṇāmadharmānaḥ / yad yāvad bhikṣavaḥ sarvebhyaḥ saṃskārebhyo 'laṃ nirvetum alaṃ viraktum alaṃ vimoktuṃ //
body.translated_text: 2. There the Blessed One addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: "Impermanent, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, are all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) — unstable, unreliable, subject to change by nature. Insofar as this is so, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, one should be sufficiently disenchanted with all <s>saṃskāras</s>, sufficiently dispassionate, sufficiently ready for liberation."

body.text: 3. sarveṣām sattvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇinām āmaraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ //
body.translated_text: 3. "The life of all beings, all creatures, all living things ends in death, has death as its conclusion. There is no escape from death for one who has been born."

body.text: 4. ye 'pi te bhikṣavo gṛhapatayo mahāsālakulā brāhmaṇamahāsālakulā kṣatriyo mahāsālakulā āsāṃ mahādhanā mahābhogāḥ prabhūtamaṇimā niṣkamuktāvaiḍūryaśaṃkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatavittopakaraṇāḥ prabhūtadhanadhānyakoṣṭhāgārasannicayāḥ prabhūtadāsidāsakarmakarapauruṣeyāḥ prabhūtamitrāmātyajñātisālohitās, teṣām api maraṇāntaṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ //
body.translated_text: 4. "Those householders, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, from great <s>gṛhapati</s> (householder) families, from great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families, from great <s>kṣatriya</s> families — those of great wealth, great possessions, abundant in gems, gold coins, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch, crystal, coral, gold, and silver, with abundant goods and resources, abundant stores of grain and treasure, abundant servants, workers, and attendants, abundant friends, ministers, kinsmen, and relatives — for them too, life ends in death, has death as its conclusion. There is no escape from death for one who has been born."

body.text: 5. ye 'pi te bhikṣavaḥ rājānaḥ kṣatriyāś ca mūrdhnābhiṣiktā jānapadaiśvaryāsthāmavīryam anuprāptā mahāntaṃ pṛthvīmaṇḍalam abhinirjityāvasanti, teṣām api maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ //
body.translated_text: 5. "Those kings, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s> anointed on the head, who have attained sovereignty, power, might, and valor over their peoples, who have conquered and dwell upon a great expanse of the earth — for them too, life ends in death, has death as its conclusion. There is no escape from death for one who has been born."

body.text: ye 'pi te bhikṣava ṛṣayo vānaprasthāḥ pramuktaphalāhārāḥ pramuktaphalabhojinaḥ pramuktaphalena yāpanti, teṣām api maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ //
body.translated_text: "Those sages (<s>ṛṣis</s>), O <s>bhikṣus</s>, forest-dwellers (<s>vānaprasthas</s>), who eat wild fruits, who subsist on wild fruits, who live by wild fruits — for them too, life ends in death, has death as its conclusion. There is no escape from death for one who has been born."

body.text: 7. ye 'pi te bhikṣavaḥ kāmāvacarā devāś cāturmahārājikā devās trayastriṃśā devā yāmā devās tuṣitā devā nirmāṇaratayo devāḥ paranirmitavaśavartino devās, teṣām api maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ //
body.translated_text: 7. "Those gods, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, of the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) — the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven, the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods — for them too, life ends in death, has death as its conclusion. There is no escape from death for one who has been born."

body.text: 8. ye 'pi te bhikṣavo rūpino devāḥ, prathamadhyānalābhino brahmakāyikā brahmapurohitā brahmapārṣadyā mahābrahmāṇā, dvitīyadhyānalābhinaḥ parittaśubhā apramāṇaśubhā ābhāsvarās, tṛtīyadhyānalābhinaḥ parittaśubhā apramāṇaśubhāḥ śubhakṛtsnāś, caturthadhyānalābhino 'nabhrakāḥ puṇyaprasavā vṛhatphalā asaṃjñisattvā avṛhā (

children.text: ) atapāḥ sudarśāḥ sudarśanā akaniṣṭhāś ca devās, teṣām api maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ //
children.translated_text: <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudarśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — for them too, life ends in death, has death as its conclusion. There is no escape from death for one who has been born."

body.translated_text: 8. "Those gods of the form realm (<s>rūpāvacara</s>), O <s>bhikṣus</s> — those who have attained the first <s>dhyāna</s>: the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, and <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods; those who have attained the second <s>dhyāna</s>: the <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, and <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods; those who have attained the third <s>dhyāna</s>: the <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, and <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods; those who have attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>: the <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Vṛhatphala</s>, <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s>, <s>Avṛha</s>,

body.text: 9. ye 'pi te bhikṣavo 'rūpino devā ākāśānantyāyatanopagā vijñānānantyāyatanopagā ākiṃcityāyatanopagā naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopagāś ca devāś ca, teṣām api maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ / traidhātukam idaṃ //
body.translated_text: 9. "Those formless gods (<s>ārūpya</s>), O <s>bhikṣus</s> — those who have reached the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), those who have reached the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>), those who have reached the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>), and those who have reached the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) — for them too, life ends in death, has death as its conclusion. There is no escape from death for one who has been born. This is the triple realm (<s>traidhātuka</s>)."

body.text: 10. ye 'pi te bhikṣavo 'rhantaḥ kṣīṇāśravā kṛtakṛtyāḥ kṛtakaraṇīyā apahṛtabhārā anuprāptasvakārthāḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanāḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittāḥ sarvacetovasiparamapāramitāprāptās, teṣām api kāyā nikṣepaṇadharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: 10. "Those <s>arhats</s>, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, whose outflows (<s>āśravas</s>) are exhausted, who have done what was to be done, whose task is accomplished, who have laid down the burden, who have attained their own goal, whose fetters of existence are destroyed, whose minds are fully liberated through right knowledge, who have reached the supreme perfection of all mental mastery — even their bodies are subject to being cast off."

body.text: 11. ye 'pi te bhikṣavaḥ pratyekabuddhāḥ khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpā ekam ātmānaṃ damanti ekam ātmānaṃ śamayanti ekam ātmānaṃ parinirvāpayanti, teṣām apy ayaṃ kāyo nikṣepaṇadharmaḥ //
body.translated_text: 11. "Those <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, solitary as a rhinoceros horn, who discipline themselves alone, pacify themselves alone, bring themselves alone to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — even their body is subject to being cast off."

body.text: 12. ye 'pi te bhikṣavas tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā daśabalabalinaḥ udārārṣabhāḥ samyaksiṃhanādanādinaś caturvaiśāradyaṃ, dharmārohaṇavaiśāradyaṃ sarvadharmadeśanāvaiśāradyaṃ nirvāṇamārgāvatāraṇavaiśāradyaṃ āśravajñānaprahāṇavaiśāradyaṃ, viśadādṛḍhanārāyaṇasaṃhatakāyās, (

children.translated_text: even their body is subject to being cast off."

body.translated_text: 12. "Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>), endowed with the power of the Ten Powers (<s>daśabala</s>), noble and bull-like, who rightly sound the lion's roar, possessing the four kinds of fearlessness — fearlessness in declaring the <s>Dharma</s>, fearlessness in teaching all <s>dharmas</s>, fearlessness in entering the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, fearlessness regarding the knowledge and abandonment of the <s>āśravas</s> — whose bodies are compact, firm, and adamantine like <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

body.text: 13. tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣavaḥ kumbhākārakṛtāni bhāṇḍā āmāni vā pakvāni vā bhedanaparyantāni bhedanaparyavasāny, evam eva bhikṣavaḥ sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ //
body.translated_text: 13. Just as, <s>bhikṣus</s>, vessels made by a potter, whether raw or fired, all end in breaking, all culminate in breaking—even so, <s>bhikṣus</s>, the life of all beings, all creatures, all living things ends in death, culminates in death; for one who is born, there is no not-dying.

body.text: 14. idam avocad bhagavān, idam uktvā sugato hy athāparāvocat śāstā /
body.translated_text: 14. Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavat</s>; having spoken thus, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Teacher, further said:

children.translated_text: Impermanent indeed are <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned things), subject to the law of arising and passing away;

children.text: utpadya hi nirūdhyante teṣāṃ vyupaśamaḥ sukhaṃ //
children.translated_text: having arisen, they cease—their pacification is bliss.
Just as a vessel of clay made by a potter
all ends in breaking—so too is the life of beings.

children.text: yathā phalānāṃ pakvānāṃ śaśvat patanato bhayaṃ /
children.translated_text: Just as for ripe fruits there is always the fear of falling,

children.text: tathā saṃskārajāḥ sattvānāṃ nityaṃ maraṇato bhayaṃ //
children.translated_text: so for beings born from <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned existence) there is always the fear of death.
All accumulations end in exhaustion, all that rises high ends in falling;

children.text: saṃyogāś ca viyogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ //
children.translated_text: all unions end in separation—life ends in death.

body.text: 15. idam avocad bhagavān āttamanas te ca bhiksavas te ca parṣado bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan //
body.translated_text: 15. Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Those <s>bhikṣus</s> and those assemblies, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavat</s>.
Thus the noble <s>Anityatāsūtra</s> (Sūtra on Impermanence) is completed.
